event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's plan to re-establish a main line of resistance to Hébécrevon is undermined by disrupted communications and the collapse of Panzer Lehr, Kampfgruppe Heinz, and the 275th Division regiment, leaving the 352d Division's flank exposed.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser hoped that retention of la Chapelle-en-Juger would permit him to re-establish a main line of resistance eastward to Hébécrevon, but he was unaware of the extent of the disaster that had overcome his troops. His command channels had been disrupted by the COBRA bombing and were saturated with overdue messages. Counting on the 5th Parachute Division, which controlled one regiment, to hold its positions near the Taute River and prevent the Americans from broadening their breach, he was not disappointed, for the paratroopers checked any genuine advance by the 330th Infantry. But Hausser also counted on the 352d Division (under II Parachute Corps) to hold the west bank of the Vire River and prevent an American penetration near Hébécrevon.
event_mentions.life_event: Hoped that retention of la Chapelle-en-Juger would permit him to re-establish a main line of resistance eastward to Hébécrevon, unaware of the extent of the disaster due to disrupted command channels saturated with overdue messages; counted on 5th Parachute Division to hold near Taute River and 352d Division to hold west bank of Vire River

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge's responsibility for not correcting Hausser's inadequate preparations and his subsequent criticism and replacement of key Seventh Army staff
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Concerned with the Panzer Group West sector... he had failed to note Hausser's inadequate preparations... Kluge criticized Hausser explicitly soon after COBRA began for his employment of the 2d SS Panzer Division... He condemned Hausser's helplessness... Kluge was certain that Hausser understood the significance of Coutances... his surprise... when he received word... of Hausser's plan to have the LXXXIV Corps... escape... by attacking southeast... Kluge's countermand of Hausser's order... Hausser's act brought... Kluge's dissatisfaction... again he countermanded Hausser's order
event_mentions.life_event: Made inadequate preparations, criticized by Kluge for employment of 2d SS Panzer Division and helplessness, planned southeast attack from Coutances area against Kluge's wishes, order countermanded

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser reports seven American penetrations and the near-destruction of Panzer Lehr. He proposes a general withdrawal of LXXXIV Corps units to Coutances while attempting to hold an outpost line near la Chapelle-en-Juger and Geffosses.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: By late afternoon on 25 July he had counted seven distinct American penetrations of his Lessay-St. Lô defensive line. He had also received Bayerlein's report that Panzer Lehr had practically no infantry left and that the division was about to cease to exist as an organized unit. Hausser therefore proposed a general withdrawal to Coutances of those LXXXIV Corps units in the coastal sector of the Cotentin. Still hoping that la Chapelle-en-Juger was not entirely lost, he thought of manning an outpost line between that village and Geffosses, the latter near the west coast.
event_mentions.life_event: Counted seven distinct American penetrations of his Lessay-St. Lô defensive line; received Bayerlein's report on Panzer Lehr; proposed a general withdrawal to Coutances of those LXXXIV Corps units in the coastal sector of the Cotentin while hoping to man an outpost line between la Chapelle-en-Juger and Geffosses

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hitler's criticism of Kluge's handling of the attack, decision to take direct control, and issuance of orders for a renewed, more powerful thrust to Avranches using additional SS panzer divisions
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Transmitting Hitler's order to Hausser... Hausser, too, admitted failure on 7 August. He ascribed the causes to the Allied air superiority, the immobility of the 116th Panzer Division, and a stronger than expected American resistance. Although additional striking forces augmented the chances of regaining Avranches, continuing threats to the army's flanks increased the chances of disaster. But since Hitler felt that the outcome of the war depended on another attack toward Avranches, there was no choice.
event_mentions.life_event: Received Hitler's order via Kluge to continue the attack toward Avranches; admitted failure of the 7 August attack citing Allied air superiority, immobility of 116th Panzer Division, and stronger American resistance; began preparing for renewed effort despite risks to flanks

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's pre-COBRA dispositions, failure to create armored reserves despite Kluge's suggestion, and resulting vulnerability of panzer divisions
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: From the night of 13 July... Hausser was increasingly free to regroup his forces... Hausser had two panzer divisions... Kluge had suggested to Hausser that he pull his two panzer divisions out of the line... Hausser, on the other hand, had been reluctant... He had consequently held the armored divisions in place... Hausser might have visualized his task... Hausser, who could have justified a withdrawal... had failed to prepare even rally points to the rear.
event_mentions.life_event: Made pre-COBRA dispositions, failed to create armored reserves despite Kluge's suggestion, held panzer divisions in place resulting in vulnerability

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Request by XLVII Panzer Corps commander to postpone attack due to 1st SS Panzer Division delays and 116th Panzer Division non-compliance
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: At H Hour--2200, 6 August--Hausser received a phone call from Funck, the XLVII Panzer Corps commander, who wanted the attack postponed. ... Hausser was inclined to agree with Funck that the news of both incidents was serious, but he was unwilling to postpone the attack. Hausser's only concession was to delay the jump-off until midnight to give the 1st SS Panzer Division two more hours to come forward. He did nothing about Schwerin.
event_mentions.life_event: Received phone call from Funck requesting postponement of attack; decided to delay jump-off until midnight but refused to postpone the attack or relieve Schwerin

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Seventh Army commander Hausser is ordered to withdraw armored divisions from the line to form a flexible reserve but takes only limited steps; he maintains a static defense in the Cotentin, underestimates American offensive potential west of the Vire, and fails to detect the COBRA build-up.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Yet Hausser was concerned... Hausser watched where it seemed more likely to begin--east of the Vire--and in doing so he failed to perceive the build-up west of the Vire... Dissatisfied with the strength of the Cotentin defenses, Kluge advised Hausser, the Seventh Army commander... Hausser's only immediate move in this direction was to detach two tank companies from the 2d SS Panzer Division and place them in the army reserve.
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered to withdraw armored divisions to form flexible reserve but took only limited steps; maintained static defense, underestimated American offensive west of Vire, failed to detect COBRA build-up

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser meets with Meindl at II Parachute Corps headquarters; Meindl's plan to break out toward Mt. Ormel using stealth and night movement.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: About 0700 that morning Hausser had arrived at the II Parachute Corps headquarters. Meindl, the corps commander, interpreted such an early visit as a bad omen, and he greeted Hausser with: "I presume the lid is on [the kettle--the German word for pocket in the military sense] and we shall probably have to try to break out." Hausser replied that that indeed was the matter he had come to discuss.
event_mentions.life_event: Arrived at II Parachute Corps headquarters and discussed breakout plans

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German higher headquarters receive first reports of American penetration south of the Périers-St. Lô highway into Montreuil and toward Marigny. Choltitz and Hausser independently commit reserves from the 353d and 275th Divisions to secure la Chapelle-en-Juger.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Not long afterward, Hausser committed part of his Seventh Army reserve, a regiment of the 275th Division, which, from its assembly area near Canisy, also moved toward la Chapelle-en-Juger. Thus, Choltitz and Hausser, acting on the same idea, sent two converging columns to deny the Americans the vital road network controlled by the village in the center of the attack zone.
event_mentions.life_event: Committed part of his Seventh Army reserve, a regiment of the 275th Division, from its assembly area near Canisy, toward la Chapelle-en-Juger to deny the Americans the vital road network

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: On the morning of 26 July, German commanders remain optimistic. Choltitz commits the rest of the 353d Division against the 9th Division. Hausser launches a counterattack with remaining 2d SS Panzer Division elements near Marigny.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, while waiting for the destroyed and virtually nonexistent regiment of the 275th Division to move northwest from Canisy, decided to launch a counterattack with the company of tanks and the company of infantry of the 2d SS Panzer Division that he still had in army reserve. He committed this force in the Marigny area, where it met American armor and infantry.
event_mentions.life_event: Launched a counterattack with the company of tanks and the company of infantry of the 2d SS Panzer Division that he still had in army reserve, committing this force in the Marigny area where it met American armor and infantry

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge's instructions to Hausser on Seventh Army defensive posture, limited German measures to create reserves by repositioning armored units, and Hausser's hesitation to withdraw panzer divisions from the line.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Yet Hausser was concerned. ... Hausser watched where it seemed more likely to begin--east of the Vire... Dissatisfied with the strength of the Cotentin defenses, Kluge advised Hausser, the Seventh Army commander... Hausser's only immediate move in this direction was to detach two tank companies... But Hausser hesitated to pull armor out of the front line...
event_mentions.life_event: Was concerned about attrition of his forces, failed to perceive American build-up west of the Vire, received instructions from Kluge, detached two tank companies as reserve but hesitated to fully withdraw panzer divisions

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: By 3 July, troop movements create flux; Germans detect VIII Corps attack preparations on 2-3 July but misjudge scale; recall 353d Division to high ground near la Haye-du-Puits.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Members of the LXXXIV Corps staff had correctly assumed... But judging that the rain would delay the jump-off... the Seventh Army staff mistakenly labeled the VIII Corps offensive only a reconnaissance in force... The real American intention soon became apparent to both headquarters, however, and Hausser and Choltitz recalled the 353d Division from Périers
event_mentions.life_event: Detected attack preparations but misjudged scale; recalled 353d Division

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge rejects a full withdrawal, fearing a rout. He orders Hausser to establish a main line of resistance from Pirou through Millières to Périers, committing all available personnel forward to halt American advances.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: He ordered Hausser to prepare a main line of resistance from Pirou through Millières to Périers in order to keep the Geffosses--St. Sauveur-Lendelin-Marigny road in German hands. He instructed Hausser to place all his available personnel on the front (rather than echeloning his defense in depth) in order to prevent immediately further American advances.
event_mentions.life_event: Received orders from Kluge to prepare a main line of resistance from Pirou through Millières to Périers and to place all available personnel on the front

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge, concerned about the Cotentin situation, suggests a limited withdrawal to free the 2d SS Panzer Division for counterattack. Hausser is only able to release one tank and one infantry battalion due to American pressure on the west coast.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: By this time, however, U.S. troops on the Cotentin west coast were attacking and tying down the LXXXIV Corps left. Hausser could not disengage the entire panzer division; by evening he had succeeded in freeing only one tank battalion and one infantry battalion from the battle. He moved these units eastward toward the breakthrough sector.
event_mentions.life_event: Could not disengage the entire 2d SS Panzer Division due to U.S. troops attacking and tying down the LXXXIV Corps left on the Cotentin west coast; by evening succeeded in freeing only one tank battalion and one infantry battalion from the battle and moved these units eastward toward the breakthrough sector

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: On 30 July, 4th Armored CCB crosses Sienne after bridging, eastern column ambushed and fights all day losing vehicles and incurring casualties; western column under Dager advances rapidly through la Haye-Pesnel and Sartilly, unknowingly passes near Seventh Army CP, reaches intact Sée bridges, captures undefended Avranches, and secures Tirepied bridge.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Three and a half miles north of Avranches, the troops unknowingly passed within several hundred yards of the Seventh Army advance command post. General Hausser, Generalmajor Rudolf-Christoph Freiherr Gersdorff, and other general staff officers made their way to safety through the meticulously regular intervals of the column serials.
event_mentions.life_event: Narrowly escaped through American column with staff; fled toward Mortain

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser arrives at II Parachute Corps CP and decides to breakout with 3d Parachute Division; troops prepared.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser arrives at II Parachute Corps CP and decides to breakout with 3d Parachute Division; troops prepared. Hausser, Seventh Army commander and in charge of the encircled forces, arrived with a small staff after dark on 19 August at the II Parachute Corps command post. ... Hausser also elected to break out with the paratroopers.
event_mentions.life_event: Arrived at II Parachute Corps CP and decided to breakout with 3d Parachute Division

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Corlett orders 30th Division to seize Tessy-sur-Vire while CCA attacks south through Villebaudon to Percy then east to encircle Tessy; German 2d Panzer Division assembles and defends the Moyon-Troisgots line.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: To protect the assembly of the 2d Panzer Division, Kluge had instructed Hausser to have the II Parachute Corps, which still straddled the Vire River, establish a strong defensive line from Moyon eastward through Conde-sur-Vire and Bieville to Caumont, where it was to tie in with the LVIII Panzer Corps.
event_mentions.life_event: Instructed by Kluge to establish a defensive line with II Parachute Corps

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German LXXXIV Corps and supporting units react to American breakthrough by withdrawing along Cotentin west coast and establishing hasty north-south defensive lines facing east to avoid encirclement
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: When Hausser and Choltitz suddenly became aware... Hausser, meanwhile, had requested permission to withdraw the LXXXIV Corps... Deciding they could wait no longer, Hausser and Choltitz agreed to withdraw to Coutances... In this situation, Hausser recommended that Kluge permit him to restore order
event_mentions.life_event: Became aware of American armored columns, realized need to move fast to avoid encirclement, requested permission to withdraw LXXXIV Corps, agreed with Choltitz to withdraw to Coutances, recommended straightening the front to Kluge

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser plans urgent breakout across Dives River amid communication chaos and clogged roads, with LXXIV Corps out of touch.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, the Seventh Army commander, came to the conclusion that he would have to fight his way across the Dives and out of the pocket that night... Handicapped by communications difficulties, Hausser tried to give his instructions on the forthcoming operation personally to his corps commanders.
event_mentions.life_event: Plans urgent breakout across Dives River amid communication chaos

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser attempts to downplay the American breakthrough while Kluge recognizes the need to stop the flow from Avranches and seeks reinforcements from other sectors.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Although Kluge was aware of the meaning of these events, Hausser, the *Seventh Army* commander, tried to minimize the gravity of the situation by maintaining that "only armored elements have broken through [and that] so far there has been no exploitation of the breakthrough with massed forces."
event_mentions.life_event: Attempted to downplay the seriousness of the American breakthrough

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser requests withdrawals to Geffosses-St. Sauveur-Lendelin then Coutances under 2d SS cover; plans hold amid Kluge's absence; unaware of Panzer Lehr destruction.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, meanwhile, had requested permission to withdraw the LXXXIV Corps to the Geffosses--St. Sauveur-Lendelin line. Soon afterward he wanted authorization to withdraw even farther, to Coutances. ... Deciding they could wait no longer, Hausser and Choltitz agreed to withdraw to Coutances...
event_mentions.life_event: Requested permission to withdraw LXXXIV Corps to Geffosses-St. Sauveur-Lendelin then Coutances, agreed with Choltitz to withdraw to Coutances

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's pre-COBRA dispositions, including retention of Panzer Lehr and 2d SS Panzer Division in static defense despite Kluge's suggestion to create mobile reserves, leading to their ineffective use.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Kluge had suggested to Hausser that he pull his two panzer divisions out of the line, replace them with infantry, and conserve them for mobile action against American penetrations of the defensive line. Hausser, on the other hand, had been reluctant to deprive his static defense of armor.
event_mentions.life_event: Retained Panzer Lehr and 2d SS Panzer Division in static defense instead of creating mobile reserves as suggested by Kluge

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Meindl halts reckless paratrooper attack, confers with Hausser in bomb crater, coordinates attack on Hill 262 from north; German artillery and infantry assaults on Polish positions throughout afternoon of 20 August
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Meindl found the army commander southwest of Coudehard about noontime. In an old bomb crater... they discussed the situation. Meindl reported his intention of attacking Hill 262 from the north and learned from Hausser that a panzer division had reached the Mt. Ormel area...
event_mentions.life_event: Conferred with Meindl in a bomb crater and planned to join a panzer division for the final breakout

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German forces withdraw into a shrinking pocket east of the Falaise-Argentan highway as Allied pressure increases, with severe communications and logistical difficulties
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: with the exit from the pocket in imminent danger of being closed by Allied pincers at Trun and Chambois, Hausser, the Seventh Army commander, came to the conclusion that he would have to fight his way across the Dives and out of the pocket that night--not an easy matter.
event_mentions.life_event: Concluded that Seventh Army would have to fight its way across the Dives River and out of the pocket that night

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's concerns over attrition in the hedgerow fighting, expectation of an American offensive east of the Vire, failure to detect the COBRA build-up west of the Vire, and Seventh Army headquarters' denial of imminent attack indicators.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Yet Hausser was concerned. The battle of the hedgerows had worn down his forces at an alarming rate... Hausser watched where it seemed more likely to begin--east of the Vire--and in doing so he failed to perceive the build-up west of the Vire.
event_mentions.life_event: Was concerned about attrition, expected American offensive east of the Vire, failed to detect COBRA build-up west of the Vire

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German intelligence failure to report significant changes in American dispositions detected by radio interception before COBRA.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Radio interception had revealed significant changes in American dispositions during the week preceding COBRA, but these were not reflected in the reports that reached army group and theater headquarters. They did not even reach Hausser.
event_mentions.life_event: Did not receive reports on significant changes in American dispositions detected by radio interception

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser reports seven American penetrations and near destruction of Panzer Lehr; proposes general withdrawal to Coutances while hoping to hold an outpost line at la Chapelle-en-Juger and Geffosses
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser's difficulty with the panzer division was only part of the story. By late afternoon on 25 July he had counted seven distinct American penetrations of his Lessay-St. Lô defensive line. He had also received Bayerlein's report...
event_mentions.life_event: Reported seven American penetrations and near destruction of Panzer Lehr; proposed general withdrawal to Coutances while hoping to hold an outpost line at la Chapelle-en-Juger and Geffosses

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser joins Meindl at II Parachute Corps CP; preparations and initial movement of 3d Parachute Division breakout column from la Londe on night of 19 August
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, *Seventh Army* commander and in charge of the encircled forces, arrived with a small staff after dark on 19 August at the *II Parachute Corps* command post. ... Hausser also elected to break out with the paratroopers.
event_mentions.life_event: Joined Meindl at II Parachute Corps CP and elected to break out with the 3d Parachute Division

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Field commanders' skepticism contrasting Hitler's ambitions, resulting in the Mortain counterattack toward Avranches
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, who considered the task of regaining Avranches relatively easy, felt that holding Avranches after taking it would be the difficult part of the assignment, to say nothing of launching a further attack to the northeast.
event_mentions.life_event: Considered regaining Avranches easy but holding it difficult, skeptical of further attack northeast

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Status of German higher commands after the battle, with most commanders including Hausser wounded, and command changes for the Seventh Army
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Most of the higher commanders, including Hausser, were wounded. When Hausser was evacuated, Funck, the XLVII Panzer Corps commander, took temporary command of the Seventh Army, which was subordinated to the Fifth Panzer Army.
event_mentions.life_event: Was wounded and subsequently evacuated

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German commanders note temporary stabilization by II SS Panzer Corps and II Parachute Corps near Vire but agree attack must launch immediately to regain initiative before further deterioration.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Although Hausser had to keep the *116th Panzer Division* committed defensively, he had pulled the *2d SS* and *2d Panzer Divisions* out of the line without breaking the connected front between the Sée River and Vire.
event_mentions.life_event: Kept 116th Panzer Division committed defensively while pulling out 2d SS and 2d Panzer Divisions

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German troop movements on 3 July, mistaken assessment of the American attack as a reconnaissance in force due to rain, and the recall and repositioning of the 353d Division to the high ground near la Haye-du-Puits, which became the main line of resistance.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: The real American intention soon became apparent to both headquarters, however, and Hausser and Choltitz recalled the 353d Division from Périers and repositioned the men on the high ground about la Haye-du-Puits.
event_mentions.life_event: Recalled the 353d Division from Périers and repositioned it on high ground near la Haye-du-Puits

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German reaction and failed counterattack by 352d Division; continued artillery fire on St. Lô
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Surprised and embarrassed by the speed with which the Americans had taken the city, Hausser ordered Meindl to have the 352d Division retake the town, but refused Meindl's request for part of the 275th Division...
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered 352d Division to retake St. Lô but refused Meindl's request for reinforcements

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Unbeknownst to Americans, their pressure forces Germans to commit reserves piecemeal, stretch their lines, and weaken other sectors including St. Lô.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Anticipating by 5 July that the Americans might break through to Périers and cut off the LXXXIV Corps forces in the la Haye-du-Puits sector, Hausser, the Seventh Army commander, had demanded additional reserves.
event_mentions.life_event: Demanded additional reserves anticipating American breakthrough to Périers

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge reacts with alarm to the bombing, contacts Eberbach and Hausser, and expresses concern about impending heavy fighting and the need for reserves
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Bayerlein's self-confidence was shared by Hausser, the Seventh Army commander... Kluge telephoned Hausser and asked for "a quick run-down on the situation." Hausser complied. He began a calm recital of facts...
event_mentions.life_event: Received call from Kluge, provided situation report calmly, agreed heavy fighting expected

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Overall German strategic gamble in Normandy despite strong defensive preparations, risks of penetration leading to withdrawal or rout, and hope of holding until counterattack or Hitler's promised miracle.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Despite excellent defensive preparations--Eberbach facing the British with a deep-zone defense, Hausser facing the Americans and utilizing the terrain to advantage--holding the line in Normandy was a gamble.
event_mentions.life_event: Faced the Americans utilizing the terrain to advantage

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Factors explaining German slackening resistance on 4 July; heavy losses and lack of reserves; commitment of 15th Parachute Regiment to stabilize LXXXIV Corps line
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Only by getting OKW to release control of the 15th Parachute Regiment and by committing that regiment at once was the Seventh Army able to permit the LXXXIV Corps to refashion its defensive line that night.
event_mentions.life_event: Commanded the Seventh Army which had to commit the 15th Parachute Regiment to stabilize the LXXXIV Corps line

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge considers altering main attack axis from north of Mortain to southwest through Mortain; Seventh Army planners and Gersdorff persuade him to retain original plan due to road net and terrain advantages.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Despite the completion of the attack preparations, it took the persuasion of Hausser's chief of staff, Gersdorff, to reassure Kluge that the plans about to be executed were probably the better...
event_mentions.life_event: His chief of staff Gersdorff persuaded Kluge to keep original plan

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Allied breakthrough to Dives River; Blumentritt-Jodl phone call urges withdrawal decision amid fuel shortages and command vacuum.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Implying that withdrawal from the pocket was becoming increasingly necessary, Blumentritt passed on the insistence of Dietrich, Hausser, and Eberbach that "an over-all decision has to be made."
event_mentions.life_event: Insisted on overall withdrawal decision with Dietrich and Eberbach

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: 4th Armored western column passes German command post, reaches intact Sée bridges, enters undefended Avranches, secures Tirepied
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: General Hausser, Generalmajor Rudolf-Christoph Freiherr Gersdorff, and other general staff officers made their way to safety... The German officers fled eastward through Brécey toward Mortain.
event_mentions.life_event: At advance command post; fled eastward through Brécey toward Mortain

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge's responsibility for not correcting Hausser's inadequate preparations, his preoccupation with the British sector, criticism of Hausser's leadership and staff, and eventual replacement of key subordinates.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Kluge criticized Hausser explicitly soon after COBRA began for his employment of the 2d SS Panzer Division. He condemned Hausser's helplessness in the face of communications difficulties.
event_mentions.life_event: Criticized by Kluge for employment of 2d SS Panzer Division, helplessness with communications, and poor leadership; his orders were countermanded

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge reacts with alarm to the bombing, initially believing it struck Panzer Group West; telephone conversation with Eberbach and Hausser reveals differing levels of concern
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Kluge telephoned Hausser and asked for "a quick run-down on the situation." Hausser complied... "We've got to expect it somewhere," Hausser allowed. He revealed little concern or worry.
event_mentions.life_event: Gave Kluge a calm telephone report on the situation, showing little concern about the bombing and expected fighting

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Lack of alternate positions or rally points prepared by Hausser, contrasted with Choltitz's independent actions, compounded by poor command relationship causing confusion, floating flanks, and loss of Panzer Lehr.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, who could have justified a withdrawal and who could have given up ground without endangering the forces of Army Group B, had failed to prepare even rally points to the rear.
event_mentions.life_event: Failed to prepare rally points to the rear and allowed 352d Division to remain under II Parachute Corps control, leading to floating flanks for Panzer Lehr

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Model confers with German commanders at Fifth Panzer Army HQ near Lisieux on the morning of 18 August 1944 to discuss stabilizing the front and withdrawal plans
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Since Hausser was unwilling to leave his troops at that critical time, his chief of staff, Generalmajor Rudolf-Christoph Freiherr von Gersdorff, represented him at the conference.
event_mentions.life_event: Did not attend conference in person; represented by chief of staff

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hitler appoints Hausser temporary commander of Army Group B with mission to attack toward Sées; Kluge reappears after being strafed and losing radio contact
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: An hour later Hitler placed Hausser in temporary command of the forces under Army Group B... Hausser's immediate mission as acting commander of Army Group B was to destroy...
event_mentions.life_event: Appointed by Hitler as temporary commander with mission to attack toward Sées

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Expansion of subordinate corps under Seventh Army from one to six by end of June, including I SS Panzer, II Parachute, XLVII Panzer, LXXXVI, and II SS Panzer Corps, with map reference
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: The II SS Panzer Corps, commanded by Generaloberst Paul Hausser, had arrived in the Caen sector near the end of the month after having been recalled from the Eastern Front.
event_mentions.position_at_event: Commanding General of II SS Panzer Corps
event_mentions.life_event: Commanded II SS Panzer Corps in the Caen sector from late June

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Detailed counterattack orders: disengagement and assembly for XLVII Panzer Corps assault on 6 August
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Kluge directed Hausser to launch an attack ... While the LXXIV and II SS Panzer Corps ... Hausser planned to disengage the other three divisions from his Seventh Army front
event_mentions.life_event: directed to launch attack; planned disengagement of divisions

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Consequences of Hausser's dispositions: Panzer Lehr destroyed, 2d SS unable to counterattack, gap between LXXXIV and II Parachute Corps
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser had so disposed his troops that the Americans knocked out one of the two panzer divisions... Without additional assembled reserves, Hausser could not close the gap
event_mentions.life_event: disposed troops so that Panzer Lehr was knocked out and 2d SS Panzer Division could not counterattack effectively

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Corlett adjusts objective to Troisgots; 30th Division prevents German counterattack
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser had helped the Americans too. Having become convinced that the *XLVII Panzer Corps* attack had failed... Hausser ordered the corps to assume defensive positions...
event_mentions.life_event: ordered XLVII Panzer Corps to assume defensive positions

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German command discussions on 17 July lead to decision to withdraw from St. Lô sector; Hausser granted permission to pull back to heights south of city
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Seventh Army had called Army Group B... and Hausser requested not only permission to withdraw... The request was rather surprising... Kluge permitted Hausser to withdraw.
event_mentions.life_event: Requested and received permission to withdraw from St. Lô sector

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German high command changes in early July 1944, with Kluge replacing Rundstedt, Eberbach replacing Geyr, and Hausser taking command of Seventh Army; Rommel remains the sole veteran commander from the initial invasion.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, formerly commander of the *II SS Panzer Corps* had recently become commander of the *Seventh Army*, taking the place of Dollman, who had died of a heart attack.
event_mentions.life_event: Recently became commander of the Seventh Army, taking the place of Dollman

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's shallow defense organization for Seventh Army in hedgerow terrain, emphasizing local reserves, counterattacks, assault guns, and adoption of 'bush warfare' tactics mirroring American methods.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, in command of the *Seventh Army*, with fewer troops but better defensive terrain than Eberbach, organized what in comparison appeared to be a shallow defense.
event_mentions.life_event: Organized a shallow defense in the Seventh Army sector emphasizing local reserves and counterattacks

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Detailed German withdrawal and attack plan: phased disengagement of panzer divisions by 6 August, extension of II Parachute Corps and LXXXIV Corps sectors, and Funck's planned night attack on 6 August without artillery preparation to reach the Cotentin west coast and secure Avranches.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: While the LXXIV and II SS Panzer Corps... Hausser planned to disengage the other three divisions from his Seventh Army front by executing a three-phase withdrawal.
event_mentions.life_event: Planned a three-phase withdrawal to disengage the 2d, 2d SS, and 116th Panzer Divisions for the counterattack

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Panzer Group Eberbach assumes command at Argentan on 12 August; XLVII Panzer Corps takes control and deploys arriving 116th Panzer Division elements to block American advance; German supply situation becomes critical.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: it had already deprived the Seventh Army of its supply base, thereby making Hausser's forces entirely dependent for logistical support on the Fifth Panzer Army.
event_mentions.life_event: Forces dependent on Fifth Panzer Army for supply

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German tank superiority (Mark IV, Panther, Tiger) versus Allied armor
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text:
[![General Hauser](:/b8f1f11c3a144223a32e86e3b74a2143)](https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USA/USA-E-Breakout/img/USA-E-Breakout-p46.jpg)  
General Hausser
event_mentions.life_event: Image caption mentions as general

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Initial attack on 3 July 1944 in heavy rain; limited gains by 90th Division against stiffening resistance with over 600 casualties; German satisfaction with defense despite ammunition concerns
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: By the end of the day, although American troops had forced the Germans out of some positions, the *Seventh Army* commander, Hausser, was well satisfied.
event_mentions.life_event: Was satisfied with the defense despite concerns over artillery ammunition supplies

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: American exploitation of German disorganization, including night attacks, closing the Roncey trap, and rapid advances by multiple divisions
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser's premature anticipation of the encirclement of his west coast forces... and his order for the troops on the left to attack toward the southeast
event_mentions.life_event: Prematurely anticipated encirclement and ordered left troops to attack southeast

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Meindl assumes command of 3d Parachute Division after Schimpf wounded; column reaches Dives River with only small group after bypassing Allied positions
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Thus when Meindl reached the Dives somewhere between Magny and St. Lambert, he had with him only twenty paratroopers and Hausser's small command group.
event_mentions.life_event: Traveled with Meindl's small group after the breakout column became fragmented

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Rundstedt's preference for Ay-Sèves Rivers line, Hitler's insistence on Koenig's line as main resistance, OKW orders move of 353d Division, reducing Mahlmann Line
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: In order to use them, OKW ordered Hausser to have Choltitz move the *353d* to replace the panzer grenadiers in the eastern portion of the corps sector.
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered by OKW to have Choltitz move 353d Division

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Intelligence on pocket exit and planned two-corps breakout attack by II Parachute Corps and XLVII Panzer Corps, supported by II SS Panzer Corps from outside.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: According to fragmentary intelligence available inside the pocket... Hausser intended to break out of the encirclement by means of a two-corps attack.
event_mentions.life_event: Intended to break out of the encirclement by means of a two-corps attack

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Command discussions on 10-11 August leading to agreement that an Avranches attack was impossible and that panzer forces must be redirected against the American XV Corps threat to Alençon and its supply installations.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Kluge had conferred with Hausser and Eberbach, and all three commanders were convinced that an attack on Avranches had no prospect of success.
event_mentions.life_event: Conferred with Kluge and Eberbach and agreed that Avranches attack had no prospect of success

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German artillery and attacks compress Polish perimeter; penetrations at 1700 and 1900 repelled; escape roads opened.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: While Meindl was conferring with Hausser, an impressive volume of German artillery and mortar fire... began to fall on the Polish positions...
event_mentions.life_event: Was conferring with Meindl during German attacks

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Meindl encounters Polish tanks near Coudehard; stops reckless paratroop attack; seeks Hausser
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Learning from the captain the whereabouts of Hausser, Meindl turned over to the captain's command the men who had joined him during the night
event_mentions.life_event: Location learned from captain

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge authorizes Seventh Army withdrawal to Granville-Troisgots line then attempts to pull LXXXIV Corps back to Avranches-Villedieu line; admits left flank collapse; learns Americans are in Avranches; notes high German losses, unprecedented fighter-bomber activity, and that Villedieu must be held.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: The responsibility for the crisis, he insisted, lay with Hausser's order for the left wing of the *LXXXIV Corps* to attack to the southeast.
event_mentions.life_event: Criticized by Kluge for ordering left wing of LXXXIV Corps to attack southeast

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge's report to Hitler on 11 August outlining the need to abandon the Avranches effort, withdraw the Mortain salient, and launch a panzer attack against XV Corps near Alençon using three panzer divisions.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: He had conferred with Hausser and Eberbach, and all three commanders were convinced that an attack on Avranches had no prospect of success.
event_mentions.life_event: Conferred with Kluge and Eberbach and agreed that Avranches attack had no prospect of success

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge confers with commanders and recommends immediate evacuation through Argentan-Falaise gap on 16 August due to insufficient forces and POL shortages
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: After conferring with Hausser and Eberbach, Kluge returned to Dietrich's command post where... he was supported by the army commanders...
event_mentions.position_at_event: Commander of Seventh Army / Acting Commander of Army Group B
event_mentions.life_event: Conferred with Kluge and supported recommendation for immediate evacuation

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hitler reluctantly approves launch but issues instructions for Eberbach to command at Avranches and then swing northeast into First U.S. Army flank; dispatches General Buhle to ensure compliance.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: He directed that Eberbach take command from Hausser at Avranches and swing from there to the northeast into the First U.S. Army flank...
event_mentions.life_event: To relinquish command at Avranches to Eberbach per Hitler's order

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Model subordinates Seventh Army to Fifth Panzer Army under Dietrich, issues detailed orders for defense of Touques-Lisieux-Orbec-Laigle line, movement of armored units to Evreux, defense of Eure-Seine sector, and rehabilitation of unfit units.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Model on 20 August subordinated the Seventh Army to the Fifth Panzer Army (perhaps because Hausser had been wounded and was evacuated)
event_mentions.life_event: Had been wounded and was evacuated

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German reaction on the night of 11-12 July, failed counterattacks, and establishment of a new defensive line south of the Bérigny road
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: That evening Hausser, the *Seventh Army* commander, ordered Meindl, the *II Parachute Corps* commander, to hold Hill 192 at all costs.
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered II Parachute Corps to hold Hill 192 at all costs

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German reaction on 11-12 July including Hausser's order to hold Hill 192 at all costs (issued too late), American repulsion of counterattacks, establishment of new German line south of the Bérigny highway, limited American advance on 12 July for consolidation, and German relief that a breakthrough was avoided.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: That evening Hausser, the Seventh Army commander, ordered Meindl, the II Parachute Corps commander, to hold Hill 192 at all costs.
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered II Parachute Corps to hold Hill 192 at all costs (order issued too late)

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: By 3 July movements (77th to Mont Castre, 353d to Périers), VIII Corps attack amid flux, misjudgment of rain delay, recall of 353d Division
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser and Choltitz recalled the *353d Division* from Périers and repositioned the men on the high ground about la Haye-du-Puits.
event_mentions.life_event: Recalled 353d Division from Périers and repositioned on high ground

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Failure of 116th Panzer Division to attack, relief of its commander Schwerin, and lack of progress
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: At 1600, 7 August, Hausser and Funck relieved him of command and replaced him with Funck's chief of staff, Col. Walter Reinhard.
event_mentions.life_event: Relieved Schwerin of command at 1600 on 7 August along with Funck

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge's desperate telephone conversation describing the chaotic command situation at Seventh Army headquarters on 31 July, blaming Hausser's decision and warning of the consequences if Avranches falls.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Who was to blame? The whole mess had started, it seemed to Kluge, "with Hausser's fatal decision to break out to the southeast.
event_mentions.life_event: Blamed by Kluge for fatal decision to break out to the southeast

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge assesses threats and commits additional 116th Panzer Division to close the gap
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: While he was there, Hausser and Choltitz were struggling to maintain a semblance of order in the *LXXXIV Corps* sector.
event_mentions.life_event: struggled to maintain order in LXXXIV Corps sector

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge receives report of deteriorating situation; Hausser proposes withdrawals relying on weak forces; Kluge orders LXXXIV Corps to Coutances-Soulles-Sienne line, plans counterattack.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: In this situation, Hausser recommended that Kluge permit him to restore order by straightening the Seventh Army front.
event_mentions.life_event: Recommended withdrawals to restore order

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Attack begins at 0530 on 3 July in driving rain; initial rapid progress slows as resistance stiffens; 90th Division advances less than a mile with over 600 casualties; Germans make a determined stand using limited resources effectively.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: the Seventh Army commander, Hausser, was well satisfied. His principal concern was his supply of artillery ammunition
event_mentions.life_event: Was well satisfied with German defense despite supply concerns

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge's disappearance on 15 August after leaving Dietrich's headquarters; worsening situation with continued Allied attacks on Falaise, Domfront, and Argentan, loss of Ecouché, and breakthrough to Dives River near Mézidon and St. Pierre; Dietrich orders withdrawal behind Dives.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Kluge left Dietrich's headquarters early on 15 August to confer with Hausser and Eberbach at the village of Nécy.
event_mentions.life_event: Was to be conferenced with by Kluge at Nécy

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Overall success of II Parachute and XLVII Panzer Corps breakout, challenges for remaining troops.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser's breakout attack by the *II* *Parachute* and *XLVII Panzer Corps* had thus succeeded in large measure.
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered breakout attack by II Parachute and XLVII Panzer Corps

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Heavy rain aids German escape; Meindl's final breakout to Champosoult on 21 August and assessment of paratrooper losses
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: that a tank unit had brought the seriously wounded *Seventh Army* commander, Hausser, safely out of the pocket
event_mentions.life_event: Seriously wounded but safely extracted from the pocket by a tank unit

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge reacts with alarm to the bombing, initially believing it struck Panzer Group West; telephone conversation with Hausser reveals Hausser's relative calm about the situation
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser complied. He began a calm recital of facts... Hausser agreed... He revealed little concern or worry.
event_mentions.life_event: Remained relatively calm, provided Kluge with a factual situation report showing little concern about the American activity

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's Shallow Defense and Active Counterattack Strategy for Seventh Army in Hedgerow Terrain
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, in command of the Seventh Army... organized what in comparison appeared to be a shallow defense.
event_mentions.life_event: organized shallow defense with reserves for counterattacks

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: On 6 August Kluge attempts last-minute changes to reinforce XLVII Panzer Corps using LXXXI Corps and 9th Panzer Division; controversy with Hausser over direction of thrust becomes irrelevant as units arrive too late.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: In contrast, Hausser desired the *LXXXI Corps* to send the armored division in an attack toward Mayenne.
event_mentions.life_event: Disagreed with Kluge over direction of thrust for 9th Panzer Division

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: II SS Panzer Corps role in facilitating escape, movement to Orbec, and assessment that internal unit determination was the decisive factor
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: it considered the corps had been a major factor making possible the escape of much of the *Seventh Army.
event_mentions.life_event: Escaped the pocket (previously mentioned as wounded)

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge issues withdrawal order on 16 August for movement behind Orne River in two nights, traffic control measures, and repositioning of forces; Hitler's confirming order arrives authorizing staged withdrawal behind Orne and Dives while requiring Falaise to be held and gap enlarged
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser was to pull two divisions out of the front at once and dispatch them to the Fifth Panzer Army...
event_mentions.life_event: Directed to pull two divisions out of front for Fifth Panzer Army

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Final German escapes aided by rain on night of 20-21 August, Meindl's column movement to Champosoult, estimates of paratrooper survivors, closure of escape route at St. Lambert, and mass surrender of trapped Seventh Army remnants
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: a tank unit had brought the seriously wounded Seventh Army commander, Hausser, safely out of the pocket
event_mentions.life_event: Seriously wounded, evacuated safely by tank unit

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Montgomery focuses on immediate objectives; boundary adjustment at Tournai; Allied optimism
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: the Seventh Army--commanded by Eberbach after Hausser was wounded in the Argentan-Falaise pocket--
event_mentions.life_event: Wounded in Argentan-Falaise pocket

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hitler's authorization of a strong armored counterattack toward Avranches with a slight withdrawal to a shorter line, leading to Kluge's plan using XLVII Panzer Corps with 2d, 2d SS, 116th, and later 9th and 1st SS Panzer Divisions
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: This plan accepted, Kluge directed Hausser to launch an attack with the XLVII Panzer Corps...
event_mentions.life_event: Was directed by Kluge to launch the counterattack with XLVII Panzer Corps

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser approves plans and assigns specific roles to XLVII Panzer Corps, LXXIV Corps, and LXXXIV Corps for the breakout and rear guard
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser approved Meindl's plan. He also issued his order for the XLVII Panzer Corps attack.
event_mentions.life_event: Approved Meindl's plan and issued orders assigning roles to XLVII Panzer Corps, LXXIV Corps, and LXXXIV Corps for the breakout

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge's orders fail to reach units; Choltitz does nothing; coastal units prepare southeast attack.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Unable to phone Choltitz, Hausser transmitted a message to the corps rear command post.
event_mentions.life_event: Transmitted message to Choltitz via quartermaster after phone failure

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Rundstedt suggests Ay-Sèves Rivers line; Hitler insists on holding Koenig's line, leading OKW to order 353d Division redeployment, weakening Mahlmann Line.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: OKW ordered Hausser to have Choltitz move the 353d to replace the panzer grenadiers...
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered by OKW to have Choltitz move the 353d Division

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Conflicting orders between Hausser (southeast to Percy for counterattack) and Kluge (holding attack and coastal withdrawal under protection of outposts); final order for withdrawal to Bréhal–St. Denis-le-Gast–Gavray line fails to reach forward units.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Choltitz had just received an order from Hausser to break out... toward Percy.
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered breakout southeast toward Percy for counterattack; later ordered to cancel and withdraw south

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German reinforcements move toward the front including the 84th, 85th, 89th, 331st, 363d, 708th, and 9th Panzer Divisions; at the beginning of August the front is relatively stable except at Avranches, with Panzer Group West (soon Fifth Panzer Army) engaged mainly against British attacks south of Caumont while Hausser’s Seventh Army is under heavy pressure.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: ...while Hausser's Seventh Army front, on the other hand, was hard pressed.
event_mentions.life_event: Seventh Army under heavy pressure

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Lack of alternate positions, poor coordination between Hausser and Choltitz, and resulting confusion in German withdrawals involving Panzer Lehr and 352d Division
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser allowed it to remain under the control of the II Parachute Corps.
event_mentions.life_event: Allowed 352d Division to remain under control of II Parachute Corps after St. Lô fall

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: 2d Panzer Division assembles near Tessy; II Parachute Corps establishes defensive line
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Kluge had instructed Hausser to have the *II Parachute Corps,*...
event_mentions.life_event: instructed by Kluge to establish defensive line with II Parachute Corps

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Appalling confusion in LXXXIV Corps on 28 July with nonexistent communications; key commanders killed or fired upon; Baum and Criegern conclude encirclement has occurred and plan southern breakout.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser was fired on by an American armored car near Gavray.
event_mentions.life_event: Fired upon by American armored car near Gavray

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Intelligence assessments of German armored strength and concerns over potential counterattacks
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: [General Hauser] General Hausser
event_mentions.life_event: Mentioned in image caption

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German initial reports and counter-moves on 25 July: detection of US penetration and commitment of reserves from 353d and 275th Divisions toward la Chapelle-en-Juger.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Not long afterward, Hausser committed part of his Seventh Army reserve, a regiment of the 275th Division, which, from its assembly area near Canisy, also moved toward la Chapelle-en-Juger. Thus, Choltitz and Hausser, acting on the same idea, sent two converging columns to deny the Americans the vital road network controlled by the village in the center of the attack zone.
event_mentions.life_event: Committed part of Seventh Army reserve (regiment of 275th Division) from near Canisy toward la Chapelle-en-Juger to seal the penetration

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's hopes for holding la Chapelle-en-Juger and lines to Hébécrevon, disrupted by unknown disasters to Panzer Lehr, Kampfgruppe Heinz, 5th Parachute Division, and 275th Division, leaving 352d Division's flank open.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser hoped that retention of la Chapelle-en-Juger would permit him to re-establish a main line of resistance eastward to Hébécrevon, but he was unaware of the extent of the disaster that had overcome his troops. His command channels had been disrupted by the COBRA bombing and were saturated with overdue messages. ... The result was an open left flank for the 352d Division, and in that condition the unit was simply too weak to hold Hébécrevon, much less seal off a penetration.
event_mentions.life_event: Hoped retention of la Chapelle-en-Juger would allow re-establishment of main line eastward to Hébécrevon; unaware of disasters to Panzer Lehr, Kampfgruppe Heinz, 5th Parachute Division, and 275th Division that left 352d Division's flank open

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German optimism on 26 July morning despite losses; Choltitz commits 353d Division remnants, Hausser plans counterattack with 2d SS Panzer Division elements in Marigny area.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, while waiting for the destroyed and virtually nonexistent regiment of the 275th Division to move northwest from Canisy, decided to launch a counterattack with the company of tanks and the company of infantry of the 2d SS Panzer Division that he still had in army reserve. He committed this force in the Marigny area, where it met American armor and infantry.
event_mentions.life_event: Decided to launch a counterattack in the Marigny area using the remaining company of tanks and company of infantry from 2d SS Panzer Division still in army reserve

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge suggests withdrawal of LXXXIV Corps left to free 2d SS Panzer Division for counterattack, but coastal attacks prevent full disengagement; partial units moved east.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: By this time, however, U.S. troops on the Cotentin west coast were attacking and tying down the LXXXIV Corps left. Hausser could not disengage the entire panzer division; by evening he had succeeded in freeing only one tank battalion and one infantry battalion from the battle. He moved these units eastward toward the breakthrough sector.
event_mentions.life_event: Could not fully disengage 2d SS Panzer Division due to U.S. coastal attacks; succeeded only in freeing one tank battalion and one infantry battalion and moved them eastward toward the breakthrough

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser reports seven US penetrations and Panzer Lehr's collapse by late 25 July, proposes withdrawal to Coutances and outpost line from la Chapelle-en-Juger to Geffosses.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: By late afternoon on 25 July he had counted seven distinct American penetrations of his Lessay-St. Lô defensive line. He had also received Bayerlein's report that Panzer Lehr had practically no infantry left and that the division was about to cease to exist as an organized unit. Hausser therefore proposed a general withdrawal to Coutances of those LXXXIV Corps units in the coastal sector of the Cotentin. Still hoping that la Chapelle-en-Juger was not entirely lost, he thought of manning an outpost line between that village and Geffosses, the latter near the west coast.
event_mentions.life_event: Counted seven distinct American penetrations; received Bayerlein's report on Panzer Lehr's collapse and proposed general withdrawal of LXXXIV Corps coastal units to Coutances while maintaining an outpost line from la Chapelle-en-Juger to Geffosses

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge rejects rout risk, orders main resistance line Pirou-Millères-Périers to hold roads, forward defense placement, and renews request for 9th Panzer Division.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: He ordered Hausser to prepare a main line of resistance from Pirou through Millières to Périers in order to keep the Geffosses--St. Sauveur-Lendelin-Marigny road in German hands. He instructed Hausser to place all his available personnel on the front (rather than echeloning his defense in depth) in order to prevent immediately further American advances.
event_mentions.life_event: Received orders from Kluge to prepare main resistance line Pirou-Millères-Périers using all available personnel on the front line

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Heavy German division losses in Normandy during June and July, listing destroyed and crippled units
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, the *Seventh Army* commander, counted eight divisions that had practically been destroyed in the Cotentin during the month of July alone: *Panzer Lehr, 5th Parachute, 17th SS Panzer Grenadier,* and *91st, 352d, 275th, 243d,* and *77th Infantry Divisions.*
event_mentions.life_event: Counted eight divisions practically destroyed in the Cotentin in July and noted heavy losses across Normandy units

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German counterattack orders, US consolidation, and halt on 12 July
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: That evening Hausser, the Seventh Army commander, ordered Meindl, the II Parachute Corps commander, to hold Hill 192 at all costs.
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered II Parachute Corps to hold Hill 192 at all costs (order came too late as the position had already fallen)

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: 3 July attack begins in rain; initial progress stalls; 90th Division advances <1 mile with 600 casualties; Germans hold outpost line effectively.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: By the end of the day, although American troops had forced the Germans out of some positions, the *Seventh Army* commander, Hausser, was well satisfied.
event_mentions.life_event: Was well satisfied with the defensive performance on 3 July despite American gains

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Evidence of trapped German force near Montpinchon-Roncey; LXXXIV Corps confusion, incidents involving Hausser and Tychsen.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser was fired on by an American armored car near Gavray.
event_mentions.life_event: Fired upon by American armored car near Gavray while moving in coastal sector

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Criegern contacts Baum, plans withdrawal; Choltitz receives Hausser's order to attack southeast to Percy.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Choltitz had just received an order from Hausser to break out...
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered Choltitz to attack southeast toward Percy to link with forces east of Vire

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's order to attack southeast, Kluge's counterorder for coastal withdrawal and counterattack; delayed transmission.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser insisted, and Choltitz complied... Hausser of course notified Kluge of the instructions he had issued through Choltitz...
event_mentions.life_event: Insisted on southeast attack toward Percy despite Choltitz's protest; later instructed to cancel order by Kluge

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German intelligence failure before COBRA; failure to inform higher headquarters.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: They did not even reach Hausser.
event_mentions.life_event: Did not receive reports of significant changes in American dispositions revealed by radio interception

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's pre-COBRA dispositions: regrouping forces including Panzer Lehr and 2d SS Panzer Division after St. Lô fall on 18 July.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: From the night of 13 July, when American pressure against the LXXXIV Corps left began to diminish, Hausser was increasingly free to regroup his forces because except for minor action the fighting in the Cotentin came to an end with the fall of St. Lô on 18 July. ... Hausser had two panzer divisions that were highly mobile.
event_mentions.life_event: Regrouped forces over ten days after the fall of St. Lô, holding Panzer Lehr and 2d SS Panzer Division in static positions

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge's suggestion to conserve panzer divisions rejected by Hausser who held them in static defense.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, on the other hand, had been reluctant to deprive his static defense of armor. He believed that "tanks formed the backbone of the position; built into the ground, they served as antitank guns and as armored machine guns." He had consequently held the armored divisions in place.
event_mentions.life_event: Rejected Kluge's suggestion and kept the armored divisions in static defense as the backbone of the position

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Consequences of dispositions: Panzer Lehr destroyed in COBRA bombardment; 2d SS unable to counterattack; gap between LXXXIV and II Parachute Corps.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: As a result, instead of having the infantry absorb the shock of the COBRA assault and having an armored reserve capable of counterattack, Hausser had so disposed his troops that the Americans knocked out one of the two panzer divisions in the COBRA bombardment--Panzer Lehr was immediately eliminated as a potential threat.
event_mentions.life_event: Disposed troops so that Panzer Lehr was destroyed in the bombardment and 2d SS Panzer could not be extricated for counterattack

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's lack of alternate positions unlike Eberbach; Choltitz's secret rally points; command mistrust; 352d Division positioning issues post-St. Lô.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, who could have justified a withdrawal and who could have given up ground without endangering the forces of Army Group B, had failed to prepare even rally points to the rear.
event_mentions.life_event: Failed to prepare alternate positions or rally points to the rear unlike Eberbach

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Floating flanks of Panzer Lehr and 352d; Lehr beyond salvation after further exploitation.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser allowed it to remain under the control of the II Parachute Corps.
event_mentions.life_event: Allowed 352d Division to remain under II Parachute Corps control, resulting in floating flanks for Panzer Lehr and 352d

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge's oversight of Hausser's inadequate preparations and failure to grasp Seventh Army role.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: It should have been clear to him that Hausser had not grasped the role of the Seventh Army in the defense of Normandy.
event_mentions.life_event: Did not grasp the role of Seventh Army in the defense of Normandy according to Kluge

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge criticizes Hausser's use of 2d SS Panzer Division, communications, and staff; restrains withdrawal.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Kluge criticized Hausser explicitly soon after COBRA began for his employment of the 2d SS Panzer Division.
event_mentions.life_event: Criticized by Kluge for employment of 2d SS Panzer Division, communications failures, and staff inefficiency

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Coutances crisis on 28 July: Hausser plans southeast escape instead of coastal withdrawal; Kluge countermands.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser's plan to have the LXXXIV Corps in the Coutances area escape American encirclement by attacking southeast, rather than by withdrawing south along the coast.
event_mentions.life_event: Planned for LXXXIV Corps to escape southeast from Coutances rather than withdraw along the coast

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge replaces Pemsel and Choltitz; countermands further orders; battle already lost by his intervention.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Kluge must have regretted that Hausser still commanded the Seventh Army on the following day...
event_mentions.life_event: Remained in command despite Kluge's dissatisfaction; orders countermanded by Kluge

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German defensive adjustments and reinforcements amid mounting American pressure on 11 July
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
