event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, the Seventh Army commander, refused, judging that the Panzer Lehr defeat made the region west of St. Lô more critical. Hausser insisted, nevertheless, that the Martinville ridge be held at all costs.
event_mentions.life_event: Refused Meindl's request for a regiment of the 5th Parachute Division, judging the area west of St. Lô more critical after the Panzer Lehr defeat, but insisted the Martinville ridge be held at all costs

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German high command changes in the west at the beginning of July, including Kluge replacing Rundstedt, Eberbach taking Panzer Group West, and Hausser assuming command of Seventh Army
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, formerly commander of the *II SS Panzer Corps* had recently become commander of the *Seventh Army*, taking the place of Dollman, who had died of a heart attack.
event_mentions.life_event: Had recently become commander of the Seventh Army, replacing Dollman

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's shallow defense organization for Seventh Army with local reserves for counterattacks, supported by assault guns, anticipating hedgerow bush warfare
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, in command of the *Seventh Army*, with fewer troops but better defensive terrain than Eberbach, organized what in comparison appeared to be a shallow defense.
event_mentions.life_event: Organized shallow defense with local reserves and assault guns for hedgerow bush warfare

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Overall assessment: Normandy line a gamble with strong terrain but risk of rout if penetrated, hoping for reserves or Hitler-promised miracle
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Despite excellent defensive preparations--Eberbach facing the British with a deep-zone defense, Hausser facing the Americans and utilizing the terrain to advantage--holding the line in Normandy was a gamble.
event_mentions.life_event: Utilized terrain to advantage facing the Americans

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Model's conference with commanders at Fifth Panzer Army CP near Lisieux on 18 August morning, agreeing on re-establishing front and withdrawal plan along Touques and Dives Rivers.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Since Hausser was unwilling to leave his troops at that critical time, his chief of staff, Generalmajor Rudolf-Christoph Freiherr von Gersdorff, represented him at the conference.
event_mentions.life_event: Unwilling to leave his troops at critical time so did not attend conference in person; represented by chief of staff Gersdorff

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Evening German order to hold Hill 192, U.S. repulse of counterattacks, new German defensive line
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: That evening Hausser, the *Seventh Army* commander, ordered Meindl, the *II Parachute Corps* commander, to hold Hill 192 at all costs.
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered the II Parachute Corps to hold Hill 192 at all costs

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: German command losses and leadership changes
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Of the higher staffs, only the LXXXIV Corps headquarters was missing. Most of the higher commanders, including Hausser, were wounded. When Hausser was evacuated, Funck, the XLVII Panzer Corps commander, took temporary command of the Seventh Army, which was subordinated to the Fifth Panzer Army.
event_mentions.life_event: Wounded during the breakout fighting and subsequently evacuated

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Model subordinates Seventh Army to Fifth Panzer Army and issues orders to Dietrich for Touques defense and Eure sector reinforcement on 20-21 August
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Model on 20 August subordinated the *Seventh Army* to the *Fifth Panzer Army* (perhaps because Hausser had been wounded and was evacuated)
event_mentions.life_event: Was wounded and evacuated

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge inquires about bombing via phone with Eberbach and Hausser, assesses situation as potential heavy fighting around St. Lô
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Bayerlein's self-confidence was shared by Hausser, the *Seventh Army* commander, but not by Kluge. ... Discovering that it was *Panzer Lehr* in the *Seventh Army* sector that had been bombed, Kluge telephoned Hausser and asked for "a quick run-down on the situation." Hausser complied. He began a calm recital of facts. ... Hausser agreed. ... Hausser allowed. He revealed little concern or worry. Hausser reminded him that the *353d Division* had been pulled out of the line.
event_mentions.life_event: Shared Bayerlein's self-confidence; gave Kluge a calm recital of the situation on the phone, showed little concern about expected heavy fighting around St. Lô, and reminded him that the 353d Division had been pulled out as reserve

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: 30 July: 4th Armored CCB bridges Sienne, eastern column ambushed, western under Dager passes German HQ near la Haye-Pesnel, enters undefended Avranches, secures Tirepied bridge.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Three and a half miles north of Avranches, the troops unknowingly passed within several hundred yards of the Seventh Army advance command post. General Hausser, Generalmajor Rudolf-Christoph Freiherr Gersdorff, and other general staff officers made their way to safety through the meticulously regular intervals of the column serials. On foot at first, later in commandeered vehicles, the German officers fled eastward through Brécey toward Mortain.
event_mentions.life_event: Narrowly escaped capture when his advance CP was bypassed by American column; fled eastward toward Mortain

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: 11 August: Kluge confers, urges attack on XV Corps at Alençon with 116th, 1st SS, 2d Panzer Divisions after Mortain withdrawal.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: He had conferred with Hausser and Eberbach, and all three commanders were convinced...
event_mentions.life_event: Conferred with Kluge and Eberbach and agreed that an Avranches attack had no prospect of success

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge directs Hausser to withdraw armor from Cotentin for mobile reserve; Hausser hesitates, preferring static defense with infantry substitutions.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser's only immediate move in this direction was to detach two tank companies from the 2d SS Panzer Division and place them in the army reserve. Before complying further, he awaited the arrival of the 363d Infantry Division (coming from the Fifteenth Army), which was not to reach the Seventh Army sector until August. Hausser might have taken Panzer Lehr out of the line by substituting for it the 275th Infantry Division, which he retained under army control immediately behind Panzer Lehr. He might have replaced the entire 2d SS Panzer Division with the 353d Infantry Division, which Choltitz, the LXXXIV Corps commander, withdrew to form a reserve of his own. But Hausser hesitated to pull armor out of the front line because he felt that "the defensive capabilities of an infantry division are less" than those of an armored division. Apparently believing that the type of terrain furnished adequate reason for maintaining the static defense already erected, Hausser did little more than clamor for battlefield replacements, additional artillery and supplies, and the sight of air cover.
event_mentions.life_event: Only partially complied by detaching two tank companies from 2nd SS Panzer Division to army reserve; awaited arrival of 363rd Infantry Division before further withdrawals; considered but did not execute substitutions of 275th or 353rd Infantry Divisions for armor; hesitated to pull armor due to belief that infantry had lesser defensive capabilities; maintained static defense and requested replacements, artillery, supplies, and air cover.

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser's forces worn down by hedgerow fighting; misperception of US build-up west of Vire due to terrain assumptions, leading to COBRA surprise.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Yet Hausser was concerned. The battle of the hedgerows had worn down his forces at an alarming rate. ... But Hausser and other German commanders expected that the Americans would be too impatient to await this kind of decision, and they looked for signs of a big new U.S. offensive. Hausser watched where it seemed more likely to begin--east of the Vire--and in doing so he failed to perceive the build-up west of the Vire. He could not conceive of a major attack in strength taking place between St. Lô and Coutances because the terrain there was not conducive to a massive effort. ... It was this that made the German surprise even greater when COBRA came.
event_mentions.life_event: Was concerned that hedgerow fighting had worn down his forces at an alarming rate; expected an imminent major U.S. offensive but watched for it east of the Vire rather than perceiving the actual build-up west of the Vire; could not conceive of a major attack between St. Lô and Coutances due to unsuitable terrain; this misperception contributed to complete German surprise when COBRA began.

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Funck requests postponement due to delays in 1st SS Panzer Division arrival; Hausser delays H Hour to midnight
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: At H Hour--2200, 6 August--Hausser received a phone call from Funck, the XLVII Panzer Corps commander, who wanted the attack postponed. [...] Hausser was inclined to agree with Funck that the news of both incidents was serious, but he was unwilling to postpone the attack. Hausser's only concession was to delay the jump-off until midnight to give the 1st SS Panzer Division two more hours to come forward. He did nothing about Schwerin.
event_mentions.life_event: Received phone call from Funck requesting postponement; delayed H Hour to midnight but did not relieve Schwerin or postpone the attack

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Funck reports 116th Panzer Division commander's refusal to provide tank battalion; Hausser declines to relieve him
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser was inclined to agree with Funck that the news of both incidents was serious, but he was unwilling to postpone the attack. [...] He did nothing about Schwerin.
event_mentions.life_event: Declined to relieve Schwerin of command or postpone the attack further

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: 116th Panzer Division fails to attack due to Schwerin's disobedience; relieved of command, division attacks late without progress
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: At 1600, 7 August, Hausser and Funck relieved him of command and replaced him with Funck's chief of staff, Col. Walter Rein-hard.
event_mentions.life_event: Relieved Schwerin of command along with Funck

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge transmits Hitler's orders for renewed attack with LVIII Panzer Corps; 1st SS elements shift to defense
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Transmitting Hitler's order to Hausser, Kluge informed him that the 10th SS and 12th SS Panzer Divisions were to arrive in the Seventh Army sector on 8 August and be committed soon afterwards toward Avranches under the LVIII Panzer Corps headquarters, which had recently come up from southern France.
event_mentions.life_event: Received transmission of Hitler's orders from Kluge to prepare renewed attack toward Avranches

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser admits failure on 7 August due to air superiority, 116th inaction, and US resistance but prepares to continue per Hitler
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, too, admitted failure on 7 August. He ascribed the causes to the Allied air superiority, the immobility of the 116th Panzer Division, and a stronger than expected American resistance. Although additional striking forces augmented the chances of regaining Avranches, continuing threats to the army's flanks increased the chances of disaster. But since Hitler felt that the outcome of the war depended on another attack toward Avranches, there was no choice.
event_mentions.life_event: Admitted failure of 7 August attack due to air superiority, 116th inaction, and US resistance; acknowledged need to continue attack per Hitler's wishes despite flank risks

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Model's reconstitution efforts for panzer armies behind Somme-Marne; admission of Allied tactical superiority by 29 August
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: commanded by Eberbach after Hausser was wounded in the Argentan-Falaise pocket
event_mentions.life_event: Was wounded in the Argentan-Falaise pocket, leading to Eberbach assuming command

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Rundstedt's preference for Ay-Sèves Rivers line, Hitler's insistence on Koenig's line, OKW orders 353d Division redeployment
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: In order to use them, OKW ordered Hausser to have Choltitz move the *353d* to replace the panzer grenadiers in the eastern portion of the corps sector.
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered by OKW to direct Choltitz to move the 353d Division to the eastern portion of the corps sector

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: By 3 July movements (77th to Mont Castre, 353d to Périers), misjudgment of VIII Corps attack amid flux, recall of 353d Division
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: The real American intention soon became apparent to both headquarters, however, and Hausser and Choltitz recalled the *353d Division* from Périers and repositioned the men on the high ground about la Haye-du-Puits.
event_mentions.life_event: Together with Choltitz, recalled the 353d Division from Périers and repositioned it on the high ground about la Haye-du-Puits

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Estimated German tank strength, intelligence concerns, and fears of counterattack
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: General Hausser
event_mentions.life_event: Image of General Hausser presented in section discussing estimated German tank strength and panzer divisions

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge assesses threats from Panzer Group West and LXXXIV Corps sectors, recognizes need for more troops west of Vire, commits 116th Panzer Division
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: While he was there, Hausser and Choltitz were struggling to maintain a semblance of order in the *LXXXIV Corps* sector.
event_mentions.life_event: Struggled with Choltitz to maintain order in the collapsing LXXXIV Corps sector

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Corlett directs 30th Division to Tessy and CCA to Percy for envelopment; 2d Panzer assembles for counterattack protected by II Parachute Corps
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: To protect the assembly of the *2d Panzer Division,* Kluge had instructed Hausser to have the *II Parachute Corps,* which still straddled the Vire River, establish a strong defensive line from Moyon eastward through Conde-sur-Vire and Bieville to Caumont...
event_mentions.life_event: Instructed by Kluge to have II Parachute Corps establish defensive line protecting 2d Panzer Division assembly

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: 30th Division prevents 2d Panzer counterattack; CCA secures Villebaudon and protects flanks against German threats
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser had helped the Americans too. Having become convinced that the *XLVII Panzer Corps* attack had failed even before it got started, Hausser ordered the corps to assume defensive positions along a broad front between the Vire River and Gavray. Kluge countermanded the order at once...
event_mentions.life_event: Convinced XLVII Panzer Corps attack had already failed, ordered it to assume defensive positions (order later countermanded by Kluge)

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge missing after strafing at Nécy on 15 August; frantic search ensues amid worsening pocket situation
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Kluge left Dietrich's headquarters early on 15 August to confer with Hausser and Eberbach at the village of Nécy.
event_mentions.life_event: Scheduled to confer with Kluge at Nécy

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Blumentritt urges Jodl for overall decision and temporary commander as situation worsens west of Argentan
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Implying that withdrawal from the pocket was becoming increasingly necessary, Blumentritt passed on the insistence of Dietrich, Hausser, and Eberbach that "an over-all decision has to be made."
event_mentions.life_event: Insisted (via Blumentritt) that an overall decision had to be made; later favored by Jodl as temporary commander

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hitler appoints Hausser temporary Army Group B commander on 15 August; consults Model and Kesselring for Kluge successor
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: An hour later Hitler placed Hausser in temporary command of the forces under Army Group B.
event_mentions.life_event: Appointed by Hitler as temporary commander of Army Group B

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Hausser ordered to destroy US forces near Sées with Panzer Group Eberbach attack; Kluge reappears after strafing
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser's immediate mission as acting commander of Army Group B was to destroy the American forces near Sées "which threaten all three armies with encirclement."
event_mentions.position_at_event: Temporary Commander of Army Group B
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered by Hitler to destroy U.S. forces near Sées using Panzer Group Eberbach attack

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge recommends immediate evacuation through Argentan-Falaise gap on 16 August due to insufficient forces and POL shortages
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: After conferring with Hausser and Eberbach, Kluge returned to Dietrich's command post...
event_mentions.life_event: Conferred with Kluge and supported recommendation for immediate evacuation

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge issues withdrawal order behind Orne River starting 16 August despite no Hitler directive; details traffic control
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser was to pull two divisions out of the front at once and dispatch them to the Fifth Panzer Army...
event_mentions.life_event: Ordered to pull two divisions out of the front and dispatch them to Fifth Panzer Army

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Expansion of corps under Seventh Army from one to six, detailing arrivals and commanders from invasion through end of June.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: The II *SS Panzer Corps,* commanded by Generaloberst Paul Hausser, had arrived in the Caen sector near the end of the month after having been recalled from the Eastern Front.
event_mentions.position_at_event: Commander of II SS Panzer Corps
event_mentions.life_event: Arrived in the Caen sector near the end of the month after being recalled from the Eastern Front

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge blames Hausser's breakout decision for the crisis at Avranches, derides OKW's ignorance of defenses, and warns of inevitable American breakthrough.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: The whole mess had started, it seemed to Kluge, "with Hausser's fatal decision to break out to the southeast."
event_mentions.life_event: His decision to break out to the southeast was blamed by Kluge for starting the crisis at Avranches

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Kluge authorizes withdrawals to Granville-Troisgots and Avranches-Villedieu lines, admits left flank collapse, confirms Americans in Avranches, assesses losses and air activity.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: The responsibility for the crisis, he insisted, lay with Hausser's order for the left wing of the *LXXXIV Corps* to attack to the southeast.
event_mentions.life_event: His order for the left wing of LXXXIV Corps to attack southeast was blamed by Kluge for the crisis

event_mentions.Sub_event_Name: Germans withdraw from Rennes overnight 3-4 August; 13th Infantry occupies city, 8th Division secures.
event_mentions.author: Martin Blumenson
event_mentions.series: United States Army in World War II
event_mentions.original_text: Hausser, the Seventh Army commander, gave permission at 2300 for withdrawal during the night.
event_mentions.life_event: Gave permission at 2300 for Rennes garrison to withdraw during the night
